video.title: Marcus Lemonis Opens Up: Depression, Regrets, & Losing Millions

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Marcus Lemonis (The Profit, now The Fixer on Fox; Camping World; Bed Bath & Beyond) in New York. Marcus says he lost about $50 million personally investing in businesses on the shows, has funded over 100 small businesses of which fewer than 10 worked out, and now gives no-strings money (e.g. $55k) instead of taking equity. He talks openly about depression, anxiety, work as self-medication, regret about not having children and about doing TV, and his push to try uncomfortable things like anchoring live news. Advice for beginners: pick one thing, take calculated finite risks, start with small side hustles and never bet the house. His next-decade idea is an 'everything home' platform with homes recorded on blockchain via Bed Bath & Beyond and tZERO.

tactics.name: Trade equity for honest time expectations
steps: When someone offers 10% for 10 hours a week, counter with 1% for 30 minutes a week
State up front that involvement tapers: a week together, then twice a month, then monthly, then quarterly
Or take no equity and give capital/advice informally, accepting repayment if offered

quote.text: let's do 1% of the business and 30 minutes a week
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Signals of founders worth backing
steps: They ask a lot of questions
They communicate without being chased and send information you did not ask for

quote.text: They send me information that I didn't ask for. They are overly transparent
quote.speaker: Marcus Lemonis

tactics.name: Fast hiring decisions
steps: Decide on a hire within 5-10 minutes of interview
Cut bait within 30 days if it does not work

quote.text: My interviews with employees are I know within 5 to 10 minutes. But I'm willing to cut bait within 30 days
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Wing walker's code for quitting your job
steps: Start with low-risk side hustles while keeping income
Stack to two or three side hustles
Leap only when cash flow is proven; never use your 401k or a second mortgage

quote.text: never let go of one railing until you're already holding on to the next
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Go in curious, not over-researched
steps: Visit businesses without prior research so you ask the obvious questions
Avoid reciting AI-generated stats to partners or investors
Make the maths simple for others

quote.text: I want entrepreneurs to go into businesses that they're interested in, that they want to invest in, more curious than knowledgeable
quote.speaker: Marcus Lemonis

warnings.warning: Taking equity in many small businesses accumulated stakes that ended up worth little.

quote.text: I started to do accumulate a bunch of little things that ended up being not worth much
quote.speaker: Marcus Lemonis

warnings.warning: Romanticising a new investment and spending lots of time early creates expectations you cannot keep, leading to conflict.
Time kills deals: when a counterpart stalls, momentum is lost for good.

quote.text: Time kills all deals. It kills the fire for me
quote.speaker: Marcus Lemonis

warnings.warning: Do not bet your 401k or take a second mortgage on a first venture.

quote.text: you can't take your 401k and put a second mortgage on your house
quote.speaker: Marcus Lemonis

warnings.warning: Over-reliance on AI research makes founders sound scripted, and the information is often wrong or slanted.

quote.text: Nothing's more of a turn-off
quote.speaker: Marcus Lemonis

warnings.warning: Doing business with close friends and family often damages relationships.

quote.text: I try not to do business with people that I have relationships with
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Undocumented non-equity investments created tax and audit confusion with the IRS.
TV fame cost Marcus a large share of his life and time; he is not sure he would do it again.

lessons.lesson: Self-aware 'shiny object' entrepreneurs should hire or partner way up to fill their gaps rather than force themselves to focus.

quote.text: I have to hire way up or partner way up because all those people need to fill the many gaps that I have
quote.speaker: Marcus Lemonis

lessons.lesson: Business is a people business, but AI makes process matter more over the next decade for pricing, sourcing, marketing and conversion.

quote.text: process will matter more in the next decade
quote.speaker: Marcus Lemonis

lessons.lesson: Try things that make you wildly uncomfortable; being a fish out of water is the best curriculum.

quote.text: fish out of water is the best curriculum for anything
quote.speaker: Marcus Lemonis

lessons.lesson: A founder's success is measured by how the business does after they leave: foundation, people and culture.

quote.text: if the business falls apart when you leave, then the business actually wasn't good while you were there
quote.speaker: Marcus Lemonis

lessons.lesson: Treat employees as more important than customers so they treat customers well.
Start with small, low-risk side hustles and take finite, calculated risks.

quote.text: If you're going to be an entrepreneur, start with something super basic
quote.speaker: Marcus Lemonis

lessons.lesson: Showing vulnerability and being bad at things on camera makes content relatable.
Mass rejection (door knocking, cold calling) builds the resilience entrepreneurs need.

quote.text: I learned rejection is a good thing
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Protect yourself from impulsive spending, e.g. giving up direct access to your checkbook.
Business ownership is not freedom but optionality; the regret is in not trying.

quote.text: Business ownership is not freedom. It's the opposite of freedom
quote.speaker: Marcus Lemonis
